root_cause.text: The sk_buff->dev field is repurposed as dev_scratch on the UDP receive path through a union, but this stale non-NULL integer value is dereferenced as a struct net_device pointer by bpf_skc_lookup() when a sockmap verdict program calls socket-lookup BPF helpers, causing a general protection fault.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that after skb_recv_udp() dequeues the skb and releases the rmem charge associated with dev_scratch, the skb->dev field still contains the dead dev_scratch value (a non-canonical integer like 0x1010000800004a0). When udp_read_skb() calls recv_actor() to run the SK_SKB verdict program, if that program invokes bpf_sk_lookup_tcp/udp helpers, bpf_skc_lookup() checks `if (skb->dev)` and calls `dev_net(skb->dev)`, which dereferences the integer as a pointer, triggering the fault. The fix clears skb->dev to NULL before calling recv_actor(), forcing bpf_skc_lookup() to fall back to using sock_net(skb->sk) instead.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear stale skb->dev pointer to prevent sockmap verdict programs from dereferencing freed device memory via bpf_sk_lookup_*().
intent_record.what: Added a code block that sets skb->dev to NULL after the WARN_ON_ONCE check in udp_read_skb(), along with a multi-line comment explaining the rationale for this assignment.
intent_record.how: This change clears the skb->dev pointer before passing the skb to recv_actor(). This prevents sockmap verdict programs from dereferencing a stale dev_scratch alias through bpf_sk_lookup_*() calls, since the device reference was already freed during dequeue. By setting it to NULL, the code ensures that bpf_skc_lookup() will use skb->sk instead of relying on the invalid dev pointer.
